note: CO2 (SN 2, linear electron-pair geometry) and XeF2 (SN 5 with 3 equatorial lone pairs, trigonal bipyramidal electron-pair geometry) are both linear molecules. H2O/H2S match in both geometries; NH3/BF3 and CH4/XeF4 differ in both.

O in OF2 has 2 bonded F + 2 lone pairs = SN 4 (tetrahedral electron-pair geometry, bent shape). Lone pairs compress the F-O-F angle below 109.5 deg (real value about 103 deg), so 125 deg is not reasonable.
P has 3 bonded Cl + 1 lone pair = SN 4, so it is trigonal pyramidal. The three polar P-Cl dipoles (delta-chi 0.9) all tilt to the same side of the pyramid and don't cancel, so it is polar.
Polar bonds give a nonpolar molecule when the geometry makes the bond dipoles cancel (CO2, BF3, CCl4). The other statements are false.
BF3 trigonal planar, SF6 octahedral and XeF2 linear (3 equatorial lone pairs) are symmetric, so their dipoles cancel. NF3 (trigonal pyramidal) and OF2 (bent) have lone pairs that leave a net dipole.
Tetrahedral with four identical outer atoms (CH4, CF4): the dipoles cancel. Any mixture of H and F on the four corners (CH3F, CH2F2, CHF3) leaves a net dipole.

C (2.5) is more electronegative than H (2.1), so the C-H dipoles point toward C, adding to the C-Cl dipole: the net points toward Cl. In CH2F2 both C-F dipoles and the H-to-C dipoles reinforce along the bisector of the F-C-F angle, toward the F side.

In a trigonal bipyramid the three equatorial dipoles 120 deg apart sum to zero, and the two axial dipoles are opposite each other. Axial and equatorial dipoles are perpendicular, so they can't cancel each other (option 2 is wrong).

Delta-chi(H-F) = 4.0-2.1 = 1.9 > delta-chi(O-H) = 3.5-2.1 = 1.4, yet Table 5.2 gives H2O 1.85 D > HF 1.82 D. In bent water the two O-H bond dipoles add as vectors, and the lone pairs contribute too; the dipole moment is a whole-molecule property.
Seesaw SeF4 (lone pair equatorial) has an uncancelled net dipole. Octahedral SeF6, with six identical F atoms and no lone pairs, cancels.
Delta-chi(H-Cl) = 0.9 < delta-chi(H-F) = 1.9, so the partial charges are much smaller. The longer bond doesn't make up for it: HCl is about 1.1 D vs 1.82 D for HF.

The partially negative O end points toward the positive plate (and the H end toward the negative plate), just as HF lines up F-toward-positive. 1.85 D x 3.34e-30 C·m/D = 6.179e-30, which is 6.18e-30 C·m to 3 sig figs.

S has 6 bonded atoms and no lone pairs, so SN 6 and an octahedral shape (square pyramidal would need a lone pair). The S-Cl dipole (delta-chi 0.5) can't cancel the opposite S-F dipole (delta-chi 1.5), so it is polar. The four equatorial S-F dipoles still cancel. Strictly the octahedron is slightly distorted, but the VSEPR name is octahedral.

With no lone pairs and identical outer atoms, every VSEPR parent shape (linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal, octahedral) is symmetric, so the dipoles cancel. This is a sufficient condition for a single-central-atom molecule; it isn't necessary (XeF2 and XeF4 also cancel).

The student's arithmetic is internally fine: with the Cl resultant at 3 x 0.5 x 1/3 = 0.5, CCl3F gives about 1.5-0.5 = 1.0 and CHCl3 gives about 0.4+0.5 = 0.9. Delta-chi arrows don't set dipole magnitudes, though: the opposed C-F and C-Cl dipoles in CCl3F largely cancel, while in CHCl3 the H-to-C dipole adds to the Cl resultant. Calling 0.45 D 'nearly cancel' is a slight stretch, but it is clearly the intended answer.

O has 3 H + 1 lone pair = SN 4, so it is sp3. O+ has 6-1 = 5 valence electrons (isoelectronic with N in NH3): one lone-pair hybrid plus three half-filled hybrids, each overlapping an H 1s. Check: 8 total valence electrons - 3 from H = 5. AMBIGUOUS (c): if H3O+ is read as H2O + H+ with a coordinate bond, a key could count neutral O's 6 electrons (2 lone-pair hybrids before protonation). 5 is the count consistent with three equivalent O-H bonds and with (e) and (d).
A sigma bond has its electron density concentrated along the internuclear axis. In CH4 each bond is a C sp3 hybrid overlapping an H 1s (H uses 1s per the Day 11 p.20 rules).
SN 3 means sp2: the 2s and two 2p orbitals mix into 3 hybrids, which leaves one 2p unhybridized.

Promotion alone gives one 2s-based and three 2p-based bonds (the p ones 90 deg apart), which is not the four equivalent tetrahedral bonds observed. The quoted slide says 'Methane only has two unpaired electrons'; it means ground-state carbon (2s2 2p2), which does not affect the answer.
Rule: lone pairs always reside in hybrid orbitals, so N's lone pair in NH3 is in an sp3 hybrid, not a 2p. The other three statements match the rules.
O has 2 H + 2 lone pairs = SN 4, so it is sp3. Its 6 valence electrons fill two hybrids with pairs (4 e) and two with one electron each (2 e) for the O-H bonds.
SN: CH4 4, NH4+ 4, NF3 3+1 LP = 4, PCl3 3+1 LP = 4, BF3 3, BeCl2 2.

SN: C in CS2 2; N in NO3- 3; C in SCN- 2; S in SO3 2- 3 O + 1 LP = 4 (true in any resonance or expanded-octet structure); O in HOCl 2 + 2 LP = 4; C in CO3 2- 3; O in CH2O 1 + 2 LP = 3. The four table ions are NO3-, SCN-, SO3 2- and CO3 2-.
CS2 C is sp (180 deg). CO3 2- C is sp2 (120 deg). NH4+ N is sp3 (109.5 deg). The two leftover p orbitals on an sp carbon are perpendicular to each other and to the axis (90 deg).
sp2 has 1/3 s character vs 1/4 for sp3. Because 2s lies below 2p, more s character means a lower-energy hybrid.

Diamond C has 4 neighbors, tetrahedral, so sp3. Graphite C has 3 neighbors, trigonal planar, so sp2 with 120 deg angles. Three of its four valence electrons go into the sp2 sigma bonds, and one stays in the unhybridized 2p (the delocalized pi system). Prompt text has stray spaces ('diamond ,' 'graphite ,'), probably where markup was removed.
Hybridization follows the steric number: SN 3 means sp2. A double bond (CO2 is sp), three bonded atoms (NH3 is sp3) or one lone pair (NH3) alone does not decide it.

SN 4 with 1 lone pair is trigonal pyramidal (Day 10 p.26 summary table). The slide's 'Trigonal planar' label for sp3 with 3 sigma bonds is a slide error; the '<109.5 deg' angle itself is consistent with a pyramid.
The sigma bonds are 2 C-H, the C=N sigma and N-H (4), plus 1 pi. C (3 atoms) and N (2 atoms + 1 LP) are both SN 3, so sp2. The pi bond is side-to-side overlap of the leftover 2p on C and N.
A pi bond is one bond whose two lobes of electron density lie above and below the internuclear axis. It is not two bonds and not head-on overlap.
Acetylene has 2 C-H + 1 C-C = 3 sigma, and the triple bond adds 2 pi. Each C has SN 2, so sp.
Each N has N + H + 1 lone pair = SN 3, so sp2. The lone pair sits in an sp2 hybrid (lone pairs always occupy hybrids), and the leftover 2p forms the N=N pi bond.
N≡N-O: 2 sigma (N-N, N-O) + 2 pi. HCOOH: C-H, C=O, C-O, O-H is 4 sigma + 1 pi. N2H4: N-N + 4 N-H is 5 sigma, 0 pi.
Acrolein C3H4O has 4 C-H + C=C + C-C + C=O = 7 sigma and 2 pi. Benzene has 6 C-C + 6 C-H = 12 sigma, and 3 pi in either Kekulé structure.
SN: CH3 carbon 4; nitrile C 2; N (1 atom + 1 LP) 2; HCOOH C 3; carbonyl O (1 atom + 2 LP) 3; allene end C 3; allene middle C (two double bonds) 2.
Both C atoms are sp2, and the pi bond (from parallel 2p orbitals) locks the two CH2 planes into one plane, so all 6 atoms are coplanar.
The middle sp carbon's two pi bonds use perpendicular 2p orbitals. Each CH2 plane lies perpendicular to its own pi p-orbital, so the two CH2 planes are perpendicular to each other.

(a) C1-C4 are sp2 with adjacent p orbitals (conjugated diene), so 4; the CH3 carbon is sp3 and has no p orbital. (b) The sp3 CH2 in the middle breaks conjugation, so each double bond's pi electrons stay over its own 2 carbons. Minor wording point: 'over how many carbons' in (b) means per isolated pi system (2), not the 4 sp2 carbons in total.

There are 3 C-H + C-N + N=C + C=O = 6 sigma and 2 pi. N has 2 atoms + 1 LP = SN 3, so sp2. The C of N=C=O has two double bonds and SN 2, so it is sp and linear (180 deg). The drawing text labels two different H atoms both 'lower left H'; it is still 3 H on the CH3.
The CH3 carbon of CH3CN is sp3 with four sigma bonds and no unhybridized p orbital, so it can't form a pi bond. The O and C of CH2O and the N of CH3CN all have leftover 2p orbitals in pi bonds.
Only one head-on (sigma) overlap fits along an internuclear axis. The other two shared pairs are pi bonds from the two perpendicular 2p orbitals on each atom, so a triple bond is 1 sigma + 2 pi.
C2 carries H, OH, CH3 and CH2CH3, four different groups, so it is the one stereocenter. With one stereocenter the molecule is not superimposable on its mirror image, so it is chiral.
R- and S-carvone are enantiomers: same formula and the same connectivity, differing only in the 3-D arrangement at the one stereocenter.
